title: Common attack vectors: injection, XSS, CSRF and malicious uploads

videos.script: Four defects, one shape. Something a user typed reaches a program that reads text, and part of it is read as an instruction. {{shape}} A database reads SQL. The defence is a parameter, and the probe is a single quote. {{quote}} A browser reads HTML. The defence is encoding on the way out, and the probe is a harmless marker that must come back as text. {{marker}} A service reads a form as a decision. The defence is a token only its own pages carry. You send the form without it, and it is refused. {{token}} And a filesystem reads names and types. You send a spreadsheet called picture dot P N G, and the service looks at the bytes, not the name. {{upload}} Every probe is aimed at your own machine, and every one becomes a test. {{tests}} Then you take one defence away, and two tests turn red, each saying which case it lost. {{red}}
